$seller_privacy_leak_fix_2026_07_28.reason: User reported that classified/accommodation adverts must never show seller avatar, display name, or @handle, and that the chat/message button must be reachable by logged-in members only — with the strict requirement that this be enforced server-side ('lock to even if user open code = not written there due not loaded'), not merely CSS-hidden. Investigated because the site already promises this elsewhere ('Identidade do vendedor visível apenas para membros' on apollo-templates' /casa classifieds/crash sections, which already gate correctly) but the actual advert-listing/detail templates in this plugin did not.
findings: templates/single-classified.php: 'Dados do anunciante' sidebar block printed seller avatar + display_name + badge, and the 'Contato' block printed raw phone + WhatsApp links, BOTH unconditionally regardless of is_user_logged_in() — a real leak, not a display bug.

templates/single.php ([apollo_classified] shortcode view): same seller avatar/name/profile-link leak plus unconditional phone/WhatsApp. Worse: the always-rendered 'Iniciar Chat' trigger + safety-disclaimer modal embedded $author_url (contains user_login) and $author->ID directly in an inline <script> block, visible in page source to any guest regardless of the safety-modal's checkbox theater.
templates/list-item.php (classifieds archive/grid card): unconditionally printed seller avatar, display_name, and '@' . user_login, plus a plain always-active 'CHAT' link with no login gate at all.

templates/marketplace/parts/card-ticket.php (carousel ticket card): same avatar/name/@handle leak, plus a chat-modal trigger button that leaked data-a-user (numeric user ID) and data-username (handle) as HTML attributes unconditionally.
templates/marketplace/parts/card-accommodation.php: no visible name/avatar, but still leaked data-a-user/data-username attributes on its 'Ver' button regardless of login state.

By contrast, apollo_adverts_chat_button() in includes/integrations.php (the shortcode used inside apollo-templates' own /casa sections) was already correct: guests get a plain 'Faça login para contatar' link with zero author identity in the markup.
$seller_privacy_leak_fix_2026_07_28.fix: All 5 templates now compute $is_logged_in_viewer = is_user_logged_in() up front and gate every seller-identity element (avatar, display_name, @user_login) and every direct-contact element (phone, WhatsApp, chat/message trigger incl. its data-a-user/data-username attributes) behind it. Guests receive a locked placeholder (lock icon + 'Vendedor/Identidade visível para membros' note, matching the site's existing copy) instead of the real data — the seller's name/avatar/handle/phone/WhatsApp/user-ID are genuinely absent from the HTML/JS source for guests, not hidden via CSS. Guest chat CTAs now link to /acesso?redirect=<back to the ad> instead of opening any modal or printing owner identity, mirroring the already-correct apollo_adverts_chat_button() pattern. Title, price, event details (event_title/event_date/event_location), and location remain always visible for every advert type (ticket resale and accommodation) per the user's explicit 'title and Event true' requirement.
$seller_privacy_leak_fix_2026_07_28.not_touched: apollo-loc's single-local.php / loc-sidebar.php / loc-residents.php (business venue profile pages) were checked and are NOT part of this leak — the phone shown there is the venue's own public business number, and 'DJs Residentes' links to DJs' own public artist profiles, not a private seller's identity. Those are a different, legitimately-public category from the peer-to-peer marketplace seller privacy this fix addresses.

$accommodation_meta_and_depoimentos_2026.helpers: includes/cpt.php -- apollo_adverts_is_accommodation(), apollo_adverts_is_hostel(), apollo_adverts_is_identity_locked(), apollo_adverts_hostel_url(). is_hostel() deliberately reads the meta on ANY post ID without a post-type check, so the /casa Acomoda strip (which lists the `local` CPT, not `classified`) can honour the same switch -- see the cross-surface note below.

$accommodation_meta_and_depoimentos_2026.lock_rule: templates/marketplace/parts/card-accommodation.php -- hostel listings render an outbound 'Reservar' link (target=_blank) and no padlock; non-hostel listings show a padlock ('ri-lock-2-line') on the CTA for guests and route to /acesso?redirect=. Guests see the thread but get a locked CTA to /acesso instead of the form.
$accommodation_meta_and_depoimentos_2026.naming: 'Depoimentos' is both the registry naming convention (15-conventions: comment/review -> depoimento) and the literal pt-BR word for 'testimonials', so the internal term and the user-facing label are the same word -- no separate translation layer, which is what the user asked for.
$accommodation_meta_and_depoimentos_2026.stay_rules_ui: single-classified.php also gained a 'Regras da estadia' info box rendering min nights / max days / availability window (dates hidden for hostels, which instead show 'disponível o ano todo').
$accommodation_meta_and_depoimentos_2026.open_divergence: ACCOMMODATION EXISTS ON TWO SURFACES and they use different post types: apollo-adverts lists `classified` posts with _classified_type=accommodation|rent_space (where this meta lives), while apollo-templates' /casa Acomoda::Rio strip lists the `local` CPT filtered by the local_type taxonomy. Unifying the two surfaces -- or registering the block on `local` as well -- is a product decision and was deliberately NOT made silently.

$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.reason: User asked to AUDIT that the HOSTEL option is wp-admin only, and that every OTHER accommodation meta reaches both the metabox and the frontend advert-registration forms, with an Airbnb-grade host UX.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.audit_verdict_hostel: PASS on visibility, FAIL on enforcement (now fixed). The hostel pair was absent from every frontend form and from ClassifiedsController's field map, so nothing could POST it through the plugin's own API. BUT apollo_adverts_register_meta() gave EVERY key show_in_rest=true with a blanket auth_callback of current_user_can('edit_posts'), and the CPT itself is show_in_rest with rest_base 'classifieds' -- so any contributor ('cena') could PATCH _classified_hostel straight through WordPress's generic post-meta REST endpoint and self-declare their spare room a public business, unmasking the auth gate. Admin-only was true of the UI, not of the write boundary.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.fix_hostel: New APOLLO_ADVERTS_ADMIN_ONLY_META constant (includes/constants.php) listing _classified_hostel, _classified_hostel_url, and -- same class of risk -- the pre-existing _classified_featured and _classified_badge. apollo_adverts_register_meta() now branches the auth_callback: keys in that list require manage_options, everything else keeps edit_posts. Enforced at the write boundary, so UI omission is no longer the only thing standing between a seller and an editorial flag.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.adjacent_bug_found: _classified_featured was ALSO in ClassifiedsController::save_meta_from_request()'s seller field map, i.e. genuinely exploitable, not merely theoretical: any logged-in user could POST featured:1 and promote their own listing across the marketplace. Removed from the map. Not part of the literal ask but the same audit question, and leaving it would have meant reporting the hostel flag secure while an identical hole stayed open next to it.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.audit_verdict_other_metas: FAIL, now fixed. The stay-rule fields were reaching the metabox only. min_nights/max_days did not exist on any frontend form. avail_start WAS posted by the rent_space form but silently dropped -- no entry in the REST field map, so it hit no meta key at all. avail_end was worse: posted as 'expires_at', which wrote the availability window's end into the ADVERT'S expiry date, so a room advertised as free until December made the entire listing auto-expire in December. Both now map to their real keys.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.fix_rest: ClassifiedsController: min_nights/max_days (clamped >=0), avail_start/avail_end (strict Y-m-d or empty, same guard as the metabox and apollo_adverts_sanitize_meta_date) added to save_meta_from_request(); all four declared in get_create_params(). hostel/hostel_url deliberately NOT declared, with an inline comment saying why.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.fix_forms: BOTH frontend registration surfaces now carry the four seller-owned fields: the [apollo_classifieds_rent_space] shortcode and the 3-step create-classified.php wizard (where the block is revealed only when the 'Hospedagem' type is chosen). UX modelled on Airbnb's host flow: one-tap presets for the common answers (1/2/3 nights, 1 week; 7/14/30 days, no limit), +/- steppers for everything else, a validated date range (end date's min= is bound to the start date), and a live plain-language summary that reads the rules back as a sentence ('Minimo 2 noites - ate 14 dias - de 01/08 a 30/09'). The two impossible combinations -- max below min, end before start -- are caught inline AND blocked at submit, so a guest never discovers the contradiction instead of the host.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.fix_single: single-classified.php gained the 'Regras da estadia' box rendering min/max/window, with hostels showing 'disponivel o ano todo' instead of a date range.
$hostel_admin_only_audit_2026_07_28.verification: Brace/paren/bracket + PHP alt-syntax balance on all 5 touched files; node --check on all 3 inline script blocks (PHP echo expressions substituted with a literal first); and a generated 9-column audit matrix asserting per key: present in apollo-core, present in adverts constants, present in metabox, reachable/unreachable from the REST write path, declared/undeclared as a create param, present/absent in each of the two frontend forms, and membership of the admin-only list. Matrix result: hostel pair NO across all four write/form columns and YES in admin-only; the other four Y across every column. Also asserted 'featured' is gone from the field map and the avail_end->expires_at mis-mapping is gone. No PHP binary in the sandbox, so php -l was unavailable.

$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.reason: User asked to audit whether resale-ticket and accommodation adverts have their CPT metas properly registered, DB-connected, and wired to BOTH the wp-admin form and the frontend user forms, with hostel admin-only.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.verdict: FAIL on the whole write pipeline. Hostel was correctly admin-only (confirmed again), but nothing else was connected end-to-end: no advert submitted from the site could reach the database at all, and even the wp-admin form could not author a ticket. Five defects, each masking the next.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.defect_1_blocking: ClassifiedsController::get_create_params() declared 'content' as required=true, while all three frontend forms post the body as 'description' and never send 'content'. Every create request therefore failed REST arg validation with a 400 before any handler ran. This is the root cause that hid everything below -- no frontend advert had ever been created, so no downstream meta bug could surface. FIX: 'content' is no longer required (a classified with a clear title and no body is valid, and every form treats description as optional) and 'description' is accepted as an alias on both create and update.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.defect_2_type_never_saved: create_item() never persisted _classified_type despite all three forms posting classified_type. Frontend adverts would have carried no type meta, while ticket-carousel.php, accommodation-grid.php and classifieds-page.php all filter on it -- so they would never have appeared in either marketplace section. FIX: create_item() now writes it, update_item() can correct it, and it is a declared create param.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.defect_3_split_vocabulary: The type enum carries two names per kind: ticket_sell == ticket and rent_space == accommodation. The forms speak the first of each pair; every read query filters the second. Both spellings are legal per the enum, which is precisely why this never errored -- adverts would simply never match. FIX: new APOLLO_ADVERTS_TYPE_CANONICAL map plus apollo_adverts_canonical_type(), applied on every write path (REST create, REST update, wp-admin save). Aliases stay ACCEPTED on input for old clients/drafts/the demo seeder but are normalised before storage, so there is one stored vocabulary and the read queries needed no change.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.defect_4_ticket_data_dropped: The sell form posted event_id and quantity from day one. Neither had a handler, and _classified_quantity had no meta key to land in at all -- so a seller picked their event and said '2 ingressos' and the resulting card rendered with an empty event block and no count. FIX: registered _classified_quantity and _classified_event_id; new apollo_adverts_link_event() stores the relation and refreshes the denormalised _classified_event_title/_date/_loc snapshot the cards read (title from the event post, date from _event_start_date, venue via apollo_event_get_loc() so the loc naming convention stays owned by apollo-events). Wired into REST create/update AND wp-admin save. card-ticket.php now renders the quantity.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.defect_5_admin_form_incomplete: The metabox had no _classified_type control and no ticket fields whatsoever, so an admin could neither author a resale advert nor repair a mis-typed one -- the only route was the REST API. FIX: type selector (showing legacy aliases normalised, with a notice when a stored value will change on save) plus a full 'Ingresso (revenda)' block (event picker, title/date/venue, quantity). Both the ticket and hospedagem blocks now reveal/hide live on type change. On save the manual event fields are written first and link_event() then overwrites them, so picking an event is authoritative while 'Nenhum' preserves hand-typed values.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.core_map_sync: apollo-core's `classified` meta map was missing 7 of the 24 keys apollo-adverts declares (type, views, rating, badge, event_title, event_date, event_loc). They still registered via the apollo_core_register_meta filter, so nothing was functionally broken, but core's own map -- the thing the registry treats as the declaration of record -- was an incomplete mirror. All 24 keys now present in both; parity asserted programmatically (0 keys in either direction).
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.hostel_reconfirmed: Hostel remains wp-admin only and is now verified at four layers, not just the UI: absent from both frontend forms, absent from the REST field map, undeclared as a create param, and gated behind manage_options in its register_meta auth_callback via APOLLO_ADVERTS_ADMIN_ONLY_META. Re-asserted by the audit matrix in this pass.
$resell_accommodation_pipeline_audit_202.verification: Generated a write-path matrix per meta for BOTH advert kinds, asserting each of: present in apollo-core, present in adverts constants, present in the wp-admin metabox, reachable from the REST write path, reachable from a frontend form, and admin-gate membership. Ticket + accommodation rows all connected end-to-end except the three event snapshot fields, which are DERIVED by link_event() rather than user-entered (verified as written inside that function, and that the function is reachable from both REST and wp-admin) and the hostel pair, which is intentionally NO across every write column. Plus: brace/paren/bracket + alt-syntax balance on all 6 touched files, node --check on the metabox script, core-vs-constants key parity, and explicit assertions that content is no longer required, description is aliased, and the type is persisted through the canonicaliser. No PHP binary in the sandbox, so php -l was unavailable.

$phase_1_2_3_registry_compliance_audit_2.finding_2_eventos_unregistered: /eventos was likewise absent from apollo-events' pages[] -- only 'portal' and 'portal/eventos' were declared, even though /eventos is the primary route. $phase_1_2_3_registry_compliance_audit_2.finding_3_feed_ownership: RETRACTED — I got this wrong. apollo-social's /feed entry ALREADY carried the correct note: 'Canonical social page - owned by apollo-templates. apollo-social provides REST + assets only.', with auth:true. safety_properties: DORMANT-SAFE — apollo_card_get() returns null unless the renderer is callable right now, so a screen can be written against a card before that card exists and lights up when the callable appears. Mirrors apollo_surface_get().
NEVER CLOBBERS — a second registration for a live type is ignored unless $replace is passed explicitly. Losing silently would reintroduce the exact fight this file ends.
UNKNOWN VARIANT DEGRADES — a typo falls back to the first declared variant rather than rendering '', because an empty string inside a grid reads as 'no results' rather than as a defect.
EMPTY RENDERER EMITS NOTHING — the '' check runs BEFORE the style call, so a declining renderer cannot leak a bare <style> tag into a grid.
REGISTERS NOTHING — no CPT, taxonomy, meta key or table. apollo-core's existing registries remain the only place those happen (02-header.CRITICAL_apollo_core_centralization).

$cpt_registration_ground_truth_audit_202.headline: apollo-core ALWAYS wins the init:5 race, so EVERY owner-plugin CPT registration for a config-declared slug is unreachable dead code. Core adds its callback inside apollo_core_bootstrap() on plugins_loaded:1; every owner plugin boots at plugins_loaded:15. Same-priority init callbacks run in registration order, so core registers first and every owner's post_type_exists() guard returns early.
$cpt_registration_ground_truth_audit_202.the_fallback_philosophy_is_not_implement: CPTRegistry::is_owner_active() (:92) — the function that would make 'fallback only when the owner is inactive' true — is defined and never called anywhere in apollo-core. The only gate is post_type_exists().
$cpt_registration_ground_truth_audit_202.consequence: register_cpt() (:143) takes only labels/public/rewrite/has_archive/menu_icon/supports/rest_base from config and hardcodes the rest. It never passes taxonomies, map_meta_cap, rest_namespace or exclude_from_search. So every owner arg outside that set is silently discarded on a live site.

live_divergences_measured.apollo_sheet: Owner wants show_ui:false, show_in_rest:false, no rest_base ('custom REST controller instead'). Core forces show_ui:true, show_in_menu:true, show_in_rest:true, rest_base 'sheets'. LIVE, apollo_sheet is exposed at /wp-json/wp/v2/sheets with the stock posts controller — the exact opposite of the owner's stated intent. Most consequential mismatch in the set.

the_fourth_wire.api: apollo_panel_register( $cpt, $schema, $replace = false ) · apollo_panel_registry() · apollo_panel_boot_registered() · class DeclarativePanel extends Panel
the_fourth_wire.what_changed: An admin editing surface is now declared with a plain array. Before this it required subclassing Panel, which meant a class file, an instantiation and a require inside apollo-lux-panels — a coupling that is exactly why only 3 of 17 CPTs ever got a real edit screen.
the_fourth_wire.why_a_registry_and_not_a_filter: A filter is write-only; you can add to it but nothing can ask it what it holds. A registry can be READ, which is what lets the schema validator sweep every panel at once, lets a harness assert coverage per CPT, and will let Phase 4 derive show_in_rest from the panel schema instead of a second declaration in MetaRegistry.
safety_properties: DORMANT-SAFE — apollo_panel_boot_registered() skips any panel whose post type is not registered, so a plugin may declare its panel before (or without) its CPT rather than producing an orphan metabox on no screen.

NEVER CLOBBERS — a second registration for a live post type is refused unless $replace is explicit. This is the guard that makes the `event` defect (two live metabox systems, the legacy one winning on DOM order) non-reproducible through this contract.
VALIDATED — every declarative panel runs Panel::validate_schema() at boot, so a malformed field is caught at registration rather than by a fatal on an edit screen.
REGISTERS NOTHING — no CPT, taxonomy, meta key or table.
the_fourth_wire.load_order: registry.php must be required AFTER Panel.php, which DeclarativePanel extends. Asserted by harness E29.

ecosystem_health.what_it_reports: Per CPT: registered vs declared-in-config, meta key count, whether a panel exists, input count, meta keys with no input anywhere, panel fields with no registered meta key, panels failing schema validation, and whether the surface and card contracts are live or dormant.
ecosystem_health.what_it_deliberately_does_not_do: It writes nothing — no meta, no options, no posts, no files. Harness E29 asserts that mechanically by failing if update_post_meta/update_option/wp_insert_post/file_put_contents/unlink/rename appear in the file at all.
ecosystem_health.why_report_and_not_repair: The brief asked for code that fixes its own channels and applies self-learning. In THIS environment that would be actively harmful: the folder deploys on save with no staging tier, there is no PHP binary and no test suite to verify a self-applied fix, and three plugins sit in the HIGH security-risk band. The stronger argument is the 2026-08-17 audit itself — the REST PII leak, the /_agent_debug hole, two fatal edit screens, a decorative admin panel, and _event_dj_ids blanking line-ups were ALL invisible while the system kept running. A layer that healed around them would have hidden them longer. Self-VALIDATING, not self-modifying; fail-closed, not fail-quiet. Adaptive behaviour is confined to presentation, where a wrong guess is cosmetic: apollo_card_render() falling back to the first declared variant, hydrateScripts() waking whatever runtime a fragment ships.
ecosystem_health.exemptions: _track_genre_legacy, _track_migrated_from and _event_is_gone are excluded from the no-input check — they are written by a migration script or by cron, and giving them a hand-editable field would be the bug rather than the fix.

$panel_to_frontend_derivation_2026_08_17.why_derivation_not_addition: Hand-writing the missing 21 would produce two files of 35 that must then stay in sync forever — the same two-declarations defect at a larger size. One schema with two renderers cannot drift from itself. Same reasoning as the surface, card and panel contracts.

design.additive_never_destructive: Runs at priority 20 on apollo_frontend_fields_{cpt}, AFTER each plugin's own definitions at priority 10. A hand-written field ALWAYS wins; derivation only fills gaps. Hand-written definitions carry human-tuned placeholders, descriptions and section assignments, and a generated field must never overwrite considered copy. The old files keep working and can be retired one at a time once proven equivalent.
design.type_map_lives_once: apollo_panel_type_to_frontend(). The two systems grew separate vocabularies — panel says toggle/media_single/wysiwyg, editor says checkbox/image/textarea. Every plugin previously bridged them by hand, which is how _dj_verified ended up a toggle in admin and a checkbox on the front end.
design.unrenderable_types_are_SKIPPED_not_downg: repeater, repeater_card, media_gallery, hours, lineup and user_multiselect map to '' and are omitted. FrontendEditor::sanitize_field() returns a string with no array branch, so a repeater submitted through the frontend would be FLATTENED and its stored rows destroyed. A repeater rendered as a text input is a data-loss bug wearing a field's clothing. That same limitation is why `track` became a CPT rather than staying a repeater.
design.capability_and_context_honoured: A field with 'cap' is excluded for users lacking it, so staff-only fields never reach a self-service form. 'contexts' => ['admin'] excludes without needing a capability, for things that are simply not the author's business.

$mockup_corrupted_generator_disarmed_202.severity: HIGH — the documented workflow would have corrupted the live DJ page.
$mockup_corrupted_generator_disarmed_202.finding: _sandbox/dj-single-page.mockup.html is character-corrupted; the 17 generated cells in styles/base/template-parts/single/ are not. Measured: 152 mockup lines carry double-encoding signatures, 0 cells do. The corruption therefore happened AFTER the cells were generated — an editor or file transfer round-tripped the mockup through CP1252 and saved it back as UTF-8.
$mockup_corrupted_generator_disarmed_202.why_it_is_dangerous: build-dj-cells.py's own header instructs: 'Edit the mockup, re-run the generator, review the diff.' Following that today would replace 17 clean cells with 17 mojibake ones — 'Cartão de artista' becomes 'CartÃ£o de artista' on the live /dj/{slug} page and inside every DJ lightbox fragment. This folder deploys on save.
$mockup_corrupted_generator_disarmed_202.exact_transform_identified: Not a strict CP1252 round trip — that was the first hypothesis and it was wrong. Bytes 0x81 0x8D 0x8F 0x90 0x9D are UNDEFINED in CP1252 and Python's codec refuses them, but the damaging tool passed them through as raw code points. U+2550 '═' (E2 95 90) became 'â' + '•' + U+0090. Confirmed by reproducing the damage synthetically and matching the real file's byte pattern.

shipped.fail_closed: build-dj-cells.py now refuses to generate from a mockup it can prove is damaged, prints the damaged line numbers and the fix. Same philosophy as apollo_surface_can_view(): a tool that cannot verify its input does not act on it. --force-dirty exists and is documented as 'do not'.
shipped.repair_path: build-dj-cells.py --repair-mockup performs the inverse transform in Python, where the C1 bytes are addressable. It is self-proving: the result is written ONLY if it strictly reduces the damage count, so an already-clean file or a differently-damaged file is returned untouched rather than mangled. Verified against a synthetic reproduction — exact byte-for-byte round trip, zero residue, correct refusal on both a clean file and plain ASCII.
shipped.range_validation: New check_ranges(). The CELLS table is line-number driven and NOTHING validated it: SUBS anchors were checked, but the five cells with no SUBS entry (progress, marquee, toast, dock, lightbox) had no guard at all. One inserted line above 427 would slide every range and emit 17 plausible, wrong cells while reporting success. Now asserts contiguity (each cell starts exactly 2 lines after the previous ends, separator blank) and tag balance per slice.

$mockup_corrupted_generator_disarmed_202.guarded_by: apollo-events harness E25 — asserts no shipped cell carries a mojibake signature AND that the generator still has its guard, its repair path and its range validation. The signature set deliberately excludes bare 'Ã', which is a legitimate Portuguese letter present in these very cells (SEÇÃO, NÃO); matching it would fail on healthy files, which is how a guard gets switched off. Validated against those exact lines — zero false positives.
$mockup_corrupted_generator_disarmed_202.operator_action_required: Run: python3 apollo-djs/_sandbox/build-dj-cells.py --repair-mockup — then re-run without the flag and review the diff. Until that is done the mockup must be treated as a damaged artefact, NOT as the approved design. The cells on disk are the good copy.
$mockup_corrupted_generator_disarmed_202.structural_parity_verified: Independent of the encoding damage, the mockup's structure and the cells still agree: CELLS line ranges resolve to the expected anchors (427 .pg, 429-437 .ev-top, 439 header.hero), and the class/id vocabulary matches. The drift is character-level only, not structural.

$quick_add_track_silently_discarded_2026.finding: DJsController::save_meta() (:509-526) built a schema-v1 track row {title,url,duration,year} and wrote it with update_post_meta(). _dj_tracks is registered with apollo_dj_sanitize_tracks_meta() as its sanitize callback, and the v2 rules drop any row missing `artists` or all four `url_*`. Every row this produced was discarded. The caller got a 200 and the track vanished — the 'Cadastrar novo DJ' quick-add track field has never worked.
$quick_add_track_silently_discarded_2026.root_cause_was_a_false_docblock: includes/functions.php:269-274 asserted that direct update_post_meta() calls are NOT routed through sanitize_meta(), and that 'WP only invokes sanitize_meta() for the REST/registered-meta path'. That is factually wrong: WP core's update_metadata() calls sanitize_meta() on EVERY write, whatever the caller. The quick-add was written against that belief. The docblock is corrected and now states the opposite explicitly, because the wrong version is what made the bug invisible.
$quick_add_track_silently_discarded_2026.fix: The quick-add now builds a v2 row: `artists` defaults to the DJ's own post title (a DJ quick-adding their release is the artist, and it is the only honest default the form can supply); the single track_url is routed to url_soundcloud / url_spotify / url_bandcamp by host, falling back to url_download, because v2 has no generic `url` field; release_date is synthesised from the year so the sort key exists. `duration` remains mandatory and comes from the form — a row without one is still dropped, BY THE ONE FUNCTION THAT DECIDES WHAT A VALID ROW IS. This block deliberately does not re-implement those rules.
$quick_add_track_silently_discarded_2026.principle_restated: There is exactly one place that defines a valid track row: apollo_dj_sanitize_tracks_meta(). A second inline copy is how the _dj_tracks duplicate-metabox incident happened. Write through it, never around it.

ghost_credits.problem: A release credits artists who may have no dj post — a guest vocalist, a remixer from outside the roster. _track_dj_ids only holds real posts.
ghost_credits.shipped: _track_ghost_artists, a comma-separated names string. apollo_track_credits() merges it with _track_dj_ids into ONE ordered list: DJs first with permalinks, then ghosts as names.
ghost_credits.why_two_flat_scalars_and_not_a_repeater: A repeater cannot be edited from the front end — FrontendEditor::sanitize_field() returns string and has no array branch. That limitation is the entire reason `track` became a CPT instead of staying meta; re-introducing a repeater here would rebuild the wall just removed.
ghost_credits.why_ghosts_are_not_auto_created_dj_posts: A ghost is a CREDIT, not a profile. Auto-creating a stub dj post per featured artist would fill the curated /djs roster with empty posts nobody claims.
ghost_credits.late_resolution: apollo_track_credits() checks whether a dj post now exists with that exact title; if so the ghost renders as a link. Nothing is written back — the ghost stays a ghost in storage and simply renders richer the day that person registers.

providers.catbox: catbox.moe / files.catbox.moe — direct MP3 hotlink, free, no account, 200MB. THE BEST CASE: native <audio>, real scrubbing, no third-party script.
providers.archive: archive.org and ia*.us.archive.org — permanent, free, direct stream. Upload needs an account.
providers.youtube: youtube.com / youtu.be, including /shorts/ and /embed/. Practical fallback. Emitted as youtube-nocookie with rel=0, modestbranding, controls=0, playsinline — the card is the control surface, and YouTube chrome inside a 15-card rail is noise.
providers.direct: any other URL, accepted ONLY if the path ends .mp3/.ogg/.oga/.m4a/.wav.

preview_audio.separate_from_release_links_on_purpose: _track_url_* are DESTINATIONS — where a listener goes to hear the whole thing on the artist's platform. _track_preview_url is a short in-page taste. card_contract_first_consumer.what: apollo_card_register('track', …) in includes/card-track.php — the Card Contract shipped with zero consumers and this is the first.
card_contract_first_consumer.style_ledger: apollo_track_card_styles() carries ONLY the new rail and playing-state rules. The .nh-track-* base styling already ships in the /casa stylesheet and is UNTOUCHED — re-declaring it would give those selectors two owners, the cardinal sin. The ledger is what makes a card impossible to deploy unstyled, which is the .accom-* defect on /anuncios.
card_contract_first_consumer.contract_bug_found_and_fixed: apollo_card_render() guarded $post_id <= 0, so the placeholder path would have rendered NOTHING. Caught in verification, not in production. A narrow, explicit exception now permits post_id 0 when args['placeholder'] is set — a bare 0 with no flag is still refused. Placeholders must go through the contract precisely so they carry the style ledger; a pre-launch surface showing only placeholders would otherwise ship with no card CSS at all.

$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.fix_2_fake_highlight: REPORTED: 'event Dismantle 2 is highlighted true? I dont remember tagging as meta cpt event of highlight TRUE'. CORRECT -- they never did. CAUSE: highlights() was ported verbatim from the mockup, including its fallback: when NO event carries highlight:true it returns featured() -- the best-ranked event of the month -- and the hero then labels that event 'Destaque'. Harmless in a demo, a fabricated editorial claim on a real site. FIX: fallback removed. No _event_highlighted, no highlight. The hero renders an honest empty state ('Nenhum evento em destaque' + how to set one) instead of promoting an event nobody chose.
$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.fix_3_arrows: REPORTED: 'Arrows left right broken with wrong border, background, shadow'. TWO causes, both fixed. Removed; styles-chrome.php is now the single definition at every breakpoint. (b) The portal now renders inside the Apollo+ shell where the Design System's generic button rules apply and were bleeding border/background/box-shadow into the pills. styles-chrome.php now states the pill owns its surface (border:0!important, appearance:none) and neutralises the icon's inherited box + pointer-events.
$phase_002_review_fixes_2026_07_28.fix_4_disponivel_tag: REPORTED: 'TAG "DISPONIVEL" IS FIXED SIMULATED DATA OR CONNECTED TO PROPER CORRECT TAXONOMY SELECTED FROM event_tag + event_type + event_category?'. ANSWER: NEITHER -- and it was wrong. It came from the _event_ticket_status META (enum free|available|soldout_soon|sold_out), and archive-event.php read it as `?: 'available'`, so ANY event with no ticket status set silently rendered a 'Disponível' chip. Not simulated data, but a default that looked like data -- an availability claim the site had no basis for. FIX: the `?: 'available'` default is gone; empty status now stays empty and ticketChip()/ticketStatus() render nothing rather than inventing a label. SEPARATELY, the card's visible tag pills now come from the REAL editorial taxonomies: archive-event.php exposes a `tags` array merged from event_tag + event_type + event_category (human-assigned in wp-admin) and eveCardHTML() prefers it, falling back to the `sound` genre terms only when an event carries none of those -- also real terms, never a defaulted meta value.

$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.severity: root-cause -- facts strip and venue (map + slider) invisible in the lightbox on /eventos and /portal
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.reported: Facts strip and venue/map appear stranded (present in the DOM, unreadable) directly under the hero when an event card opens in the lightbox, but render correctly on /evento/{slug}.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.root_cause: apollo-single-event.js's initAnim()/bindDjRail() create every ScrollTrigger (facts+panels reveal, hero parallax, footer parallax, word reveal, DJ rail pin, DJ cards) with no `scroller` option, so they all default to `scroller: window`. On the real page the window scrolls and they fire normally. Inside the lightbox the fragment mounts in `.ev-lb-scroll`, a native overflow-y:auto panel; the document is Lenis-locked and the window never moves, so those triggers can never resolve and the affected elements stay at their GSAP inline `opacity:0` forever. A second, independent gap made this invisible to the existing safety nets: bootstrap.php's unstrand() pass and the CSS floor in styles-lightbox.php both queried only the class `.ev-reveal`, which no single-event template actually applies -- the real reveal targets (.ev-fact, .ev-panel, [data-ev=access/about], .ev-spotify, .ev-gallery, .v-slider, .ev-map, .ev-vbody, .ev-dj) are a separate, hardcoded selector list inline in the JS, so both nets matched zero nodes and were dead code for this exact symptom.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.fix: (A) Instance now resolves `this.scroller = root.closest('.ev-lb-scroll') || undefined` once at construction and passes `scroller: self.scroller` to all 6 ScrollTrigger configs; undefined on /evento/{slug} and inline embeds, so behaviour there is unchanged, byte for byte. (B) Widened bootstrap.php's unstrand() query and styles-lightbox.php's CSS floor to the same selector list initAnim() actually reveals, as a belt-and-braces layer for anything that still slips through (e.g. a late image reflow). Selector is duplicated by hand in three places (apollo-single-event.js, bootstrap.php, styles-lightbox.php) -- keep them in sync if the reveal list changes.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.why_not_scrollerProxy_alone: bootstrap.php already registers `ScrollTrigger.scrollerProxy('.ev-lb-scroll', {...})`, but a proxy only supplies custom get/set methods for a scroller identifier -- it does not retroactively re-target ScrollTriggers that were created with `scroller: window` (the default). Every trigger must still be told `scroller: panel` explicitly at creation time, which is exactly what was missing.
$lightbox_reveal_scroller_fix_2026_08_01.verification: Structural: confirmed via grep that no template-part applies class `ev-reveal` to any node (facts.php inspected directly); confirmed apollo-single-event.js had exactly 6 scrollTrigger call sites, all now carrying `scroller: self.scroller`. $reader_surface_white_and_hydration_2026.scope: The shared lightbox — every surface, not just events. Version bump 1.7.1 -> 1.7.2.
$reader_surface_white_and_hydration_2026.requirement: The surface behind a fragment is solid #fff, always, in both themes. Never a token that can flip, never rgba with alpha, never a blur that lets the page behind read through. A close control is always present.

defect_1_panel_was_not_white.effect: In dark mode the reader panel rendered #0b0b0d — near black. The requirement had been silently violated on every dark-theme install since the lightbox shipped.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.the_trap: Pinning `background` alone produces WHITE TEXT ON WHITE, because --ev-ink inverts independently of --ev-bg. That renders as a blank panel with a working close button — visually identical to the 2026-08-07 stale-asset failure and considerably harder to diagnose a second time. The whole local --ev-* block has to be pinned together or not at all.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.fix: portal/styles-lightbox.php pins --ev-bg/--ev-ink/--ev-mute/--ev-faint/--ev-line/--ev-line2/--ev-soft to their resolved light-theme literals and sets background:#fff on .ev-lb-panel. Component-scoped custom properties, the form the DS blesses — NOT a :root entry.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.ownership: styles-lightbox.php is now the DECLARED LAST-WORD OWNER of the reader surface colour (.ev-lb-panel background + token pin, .ev-lb-bd background). The base sheet keeps its own values as the standalone-page default and is out-specified by the doubled selector. Do not edit both — that is the cardinal sin.
defect_1_panel_was_not_white.trade_off_accepted: Dark-mode readers get a light document panel. Deliberate: the fragment is a document, not chrome.

$reader_surface_white_and_hydration_2026.defect_2_backdrop_had_alpha: `.ev-lb-bd` was rgba(var(--rgb-diff),.72). The comment above it claimed nothing shows through a full-bleed panel — true once open, false for the ~520ms the panel is still transitioning from opacity:0, during which the backdrop IS the surface. Now an opaque #fff literal with backdrop-filter:none.

defect_3_nested_css_comment.what: :root { --ev-max: 440px }  followed by an inline /* … */ annotation INSIDE an already-open comment block. CSS comments do not nest, so the outer block terminated at that inner close.
defect_3_nested_css_comment.effect: A .ev-wrap width rule and fourteen lines of English prose were handed to the CSS parser as source. The .ev-wrap rule escaped unscoped into the global cascade — reaching the real /evento/{slug} page, not just the lightbox — and the prose survived only on the parser's silent error recovery.
defect_3_nested_css_comment.why_it_survived: Syntax highlighters DO nest comments; browsers do not. It read as a comment in every editor for months. That gap is why assertion E24 is mechanical rather than a review note.
defect_3_nested_css_comment.fix: Inner annotation rewritten without comment syntax. E24 now scans every styles*.php cell in the portal directory for a second opener inside an open span.

feature_fragment_hydration.problem: innerHTML never executes <script>. For events that was correct and documented — the event fragment's only script is an inert application/json config block and its behaviour comes from ApolloEventSingle.mount(). It stopped being the whole story the moment a second surface existed: apollo-djs ships its runtime as an inline IIFE in its `scripts` cell, and that cell is GENERATED by _sandbox/build-dj-cells.py with a do-not-hand-edit banner. A DJ fragment therefore injected as correct but DEAD html — no dock, no reveals, no shares, no scroll progress.
feature_fragment_hydration.rejected_design: A per-surface mount() API. It would have required hand-editing exactly the generated cell that must not be hand-edited, once per surface, forever.
feature_fragment_hydration.shipped: hydrateScripts() in assets/js/apollo-event-lightbox.js re-creates the fragment's own <script> nodes so the browser executes them. Zero per-plugin work, works for every surface that will ever be registered.
safety: Order preserved; a src= script blocks the ones after it, re-creating the guarantee a parsed document gives for free.
state.injectToken generation counter — a superseded fragment's async chain detects it lost and stands down, so two fast opens cannot interleave two runtimes.
EXECUTABLE allow-list — application/json and application/ld+json are data and are left alone.
Per-script failure containment; a detached node is skipped rather than aborting the chain.

KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: document-level listeners bound by a fragment runtime outlive the panel, because unmountCurrent() removes their targets but not the listeners. Their selector lookups then resolve to null and the handlers no-op. Revisit if a surface ever binds something with side effects that survive its own DOM.
feature_fragment_hydration.event_path_untouched: ApolloEventSingle.mount() still runs exactly as before. Hydration is a no-op for events.

$mockup_parity_not_verifiable_2026_08_17.missing_2_no_cell_structure: apollo-loc never went through the cell treatment. styles/base/single-local.php is a monolith with its per-item context inline at the top (_local_name, address, coords, … from line 31), exactly the shape apollo-djs moved away from. $mockup_parity_not_verifiable_2026_08_17.consequence: The loc surface in includes/surface.php stays correctly DORMANT — apollo_surface_get('loc') returns null, so no REST fragment route is registered and apollo_surface_open_attrs('loc',$id) returns ''. what_would_make_it_verifiable: 1. Copy the approved loc-single-page.html into apollo-loc/_sandbox/ so the design has a home in the repo, as apollo-djs did.
2. Extract apollo_loc_single_context( int $id ): array out of styles/base/single-local.php; the template extract()s it. Rendered output must not change — that is the whole test.
3. Add apollo_loc_render_single() + apollo_loc_can_view(). The surface, its REST fragment and the lightbox then light up together with no further wiring.

apollo-soundcloud.description: One SoundCloud player for the whole ecosystem. Apollo's own UI driving a hidden Widget-API iframe, with preview (25-65%) and full modes. Replaces seven hand-rolled implementations.

seven_implementations_found: apollo-djs/assets/js/dj-single.js:41 — full SC.Widget with vinyl binding
apollo-users/templates/single-profile.php:3815-3859 — full SC.Widget INLINE in a template
apollo-users/assets/js/profile.js:202-236 — ANOTHER SC.Widget in the same plugin
apollo-hub/assets/js/home/radio.js:29-74 — lazy api.js + its own SC.Widget
compounding_defects: api.js loaded from THREE places (single-dj.php:162, single-profile.php:103, lazily in radio.js) — a page carrying two of them loads the SDK twice.

The widget-URL string was assembled by hand FOUR times with different colours, auto_play values and chrome toggles, so one track looked and behaved differently depending on which screen you found it on.
TWO HARDCODED TRACK IDS shipping in production: apollo-dashboard/.../panel-feed.php:211 -> 1293057640 and apollo-hub/.../radio.php:28 -> 293. Neither comes from data.
Seven independent widgets cannot enforce 'only one thing plays at a time' — none of them knew the others existed. That is a requirement for a social network, not a nicety.
why.same_defect_shape: Identical to the four accommodation cards and the five Out Now sections: no single owner. See STRATEGY-integration.md §1.

api_access_reality.finding: SoundCloud CLOSED open API registration. Access is application-only through a form on developers.soundcloud.com, reviewed manually, selective, and can take weeks. Credentials cannot be assumed.
api_access_reality.verified: Web search 2026-08-17 — developers.soundcloud.com, soundcloud/api issue #219, publicapis.io/soundcloud-api.
api_access_reality.consequence: The Widget API is the PRIMARY architecture here, NOT a fallback. It needs no credentials, works for everyone today, and is the only way to implement a percentage-based preview at all — that requires getDuration(), which a bare iframe cannot report. oEmbed likewise needs no credentials and supplies title/author/artwork.
api_access_reality.the_seam: apollo_sc_provider() returns 'widget' today and 'api' if credentials ever arrive. Direct stream URLs would then replace the iframe with ZERO call-site changes. That seam is why the closed registration is an inconvenience rather than a blocker.
api_access_reality.on_the_selfhosted_repos: Navidrome, Koel, Ampache and Funkwhale are excellent self-hosted MUSIC SERVERS — they host your own audio and none of them plays a SoundCloud track. They answer a different question ('host our own catalogue') and would slot in as a second provider behind the same seam if that becomes the goal. They do not substitute for SoundCloud playback.

architecture.public_api: apollo_soundcloud_player( $url, [mode, variant, start_pct, end_pct, autoplay] ) — the only entry point. Consumers never know which transport is active.
architecture.preview_enforcement: There is no SoundCloud API for 'play from A to B'. READY -> getDuration() -> compute window -> seekTo(start) -> play() -> watch PLAY_PROGRESS and pause at end. Implemented in the runtime, not in PHP, because duration is only knowable after READY.
architecture.short_track_floor: Tracks under APOLLO_SC_PREVIEW_MIN_SECONDS (20s) play whole even in preview mode — a 4-second ID clip has no meaningful middle 40%.
architecture.lazy_everything: The SDK loads once on first play (replacing three eager loads), the iframe is created on first play (fifteen players on /casa would otherwise mean fifteen SoundCloud connections before anyone clicked), and metadata is fetched after paint.
architecture.single_active_player: The runtime holds one `current` reference and stops it before starting another; it also listens for apollo:audio:play so a catbox/YouTube track preview silences it.
architecture.progress_bar_is_honest: In preview mode the bar shows the WHOLE track with the window marked, not a 0-100% bar of the excerpt. A bar that fills completely on a 40% slice tells the listener they heard the whole thing, which is false.
architecture.degrades_honestly: If the SDK is blocked — ad blockers and privacy extensions block w.soundcloud.com often enough that this is a normal path — the hidden transport is revealed as the real, visible embed and the Apollo button is hidden. A dead play button is worse than SoundCloud's own chrome appearing. <noscript> carries the same embed.

$fsx_token_compat_2026_07_28.severity: ROOT CAUSE — explains the majority of 'one ton of elements' wrong across every Apollo+ screen
$fsx_token_compat_2026_07_28.finding: The Design System component CSS (ds-components.css / market.css, verbatim from uni.theme.v2.1.css) sizes nearly everything through calc(Npx * var(--fsx)): .a-eve-title, .a-eve-date-day, .a-eve-tag, .date-day, .date-month, .event-action .status, .stat-value and dozens more. core.js injects --fs-u and --fs-r but NOT --fsx -- in the mockup that token comes from the page's own :root, which we deliberately do not port. Every one of those calc() expressions was therefore INVALID, and CSS drops an invalid declaration entirely, so each element silently fell back to inherited sizing.
$fsx_token_compat_2026_07_28.measured_proof: Verified in a real browser (Claude in Chrome, cache-busted URL, logged-in session): getComputedStyle(document.documentElement) returned --fsx as MISSING while --fs-u was 1; .event-action .status computed to 17.69px where the DS specifies calc(var(--fsx) * .58rem) ~ 9px. Before/after screenshots confirm the same DOM going from truncated title + oversized badge + hidden venue meta to correct scale.
$fsx_token_compat_2026_07_28.why_it_looked_like_many_bugs: A single missing token degrades every sized element at once, which reads as 'the whole screen is wrong' rather than one defect. Three previous rounds chased individual symptoms (card background, arrows, badge) because the shared cause was invisible without computing styles in a real browser.
$fsx_token_compat_2026_07_28.fix: New apollo-plus-token-compat style block in aside-styles.php: .ax-body,.ax-shell,body{--fsx: var(--fs-u, var(--fs-r, 1))}. Declared on the shell's own classes, NOT on :root -- core.js owns :root and that rule stands. It inherits to every descendant so it repairs the whole component set at once, and defers automatically to a real --fsx the moment core.js ships one.
$fsx_token_compat_2026_07_28.applies_to: Every phase. Any screen in 003-011 that renders DS components depends on this token; without it they would each have reproduced the same failure.

items.issue: Hardcoded Windows debug path in production code
items.detail: file_put_contents('C:/Users/User/Local Sites/apollorio/...') hardcoded debug write. Will fail silently on any non-Windows or non-matching path server. Must be removed or gated behind if (WP_DEBUG).

items.detail: Lines L1191 and L1193 contain direct variable interpolation in SQL queries. SQL injection risk.
items.fix: Wrap all SQL queries with $wpdb->prepare() and use placeholders (%s, %d)

items.detail: Plugin.php L1185 and Admin.php L304 have raw SQL with variable interpolation.
items.fix: Use $wpdb->prepare() for all parameterized queries

items.detail: Deactivation.php L56 uses direct variable in SQL query.
items.fix: Use $wpdb->prepare() even in deactivation/cleanup hooks

items.issue: Nonces exposed in data-* HTML attributes
items.detail: 10 instances across 9 plugins where WordPress nonces are output as data-* attribute values in rendered HTML. Nonces should only be in JS config blocks (wp_json_encode) for logged-in users, never in the DOM.
items.fix: Move nonces to wp_json_encode() JS config block, guard with is_user_logged_in(), remove from data-* attributes

items.detail: At least one REST endpoint in apollo-groups uses __return_true as permission_callback, allowing unauthenticated mutations.
items.fix: Replace __return_true with proper capability check (is_user_logged_in, current_user_can, etc.) on all write endpoints

items.issue: Missing CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER on Instagram profile cURL
items.detail: get_instagram_profile_pic() method fetches Instagram avatar without CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = true. Man-in-the-middle attack risk on profile picture fetching.
items.fix: Add curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, true) to the cURL setup

items.detail: 6 HIGH unescaped echo instances across apollo-djs templates. Output not wrapped in esc_html() or esc_attr().
items.fix: Wrap all dynamic template output with appropriate escape functions: esc_html(), esc_attr(), esc_url(), wp_kses_post()

items.detail: Admin dashboard template has unescaped dynamic output.
items.fix: Use esc_html() or esc_attr() on all echoed values

items.detail: Digital signature stamp template outputs dynamic data without escaping.

DIFFERENT TOPBAR CSS SOURCE, so the two shells drifted independently. This is also why the topbar was completely unstyled on every path-B screen until 2026-07-30 (apollo_plus_open never loaded any topbar CSS at all).
Mixing A and B on one request emits two <head>/<body> pairs — already documented as a live failure in comunas.php, apollo-events Plugin.php and apollo-adverts Plugin.php.

$mu_plugins.description: Must-Use plugins in wp-content/mu-plugins/. Loaded before regular plugins, in ALPHABETICAL filename order, and cannot be deactivated from wp-admin. This is the Apollo boot layer.
$mu_plugins.$load_order_note: WordPress loads mu-plugins alphabetically; there is no dependency resolution. apollo-brain.php sorts first among the apollo-* files, which is why it can hook muplugins_loaded at -100 and still define APOLLO_REGISTRY_PATH before anything reads it. Renaming a file here silently changes boot order.
$boot_sequence: 1. WP loads every mu-plugin file alphabetically (apollo-brain → apollo-debug → apollo-dev-routing → apollo-error-handler → apollo-events-helpers-guard → apollo-force-open-registration → apollo-htaccess-lock → apollo-locale-pt-br → apollo-route-setup → apollo-webp-force → elementor-safe-mode → endurance-page-cache → force-load-apollo-events → force-load-apollo-login → force-load-apollo-telegram → force-load-apollo-templates)
2. apollo-brain hooks muplugins_loaded @ -100 → defines APOLLO_REGISTRY_PATH, require_once apollo-core.php
3. apollo-core registers its own bootstrap on plugins_loaded @ 1 (CPT/Meta/security init happens THERE, not in the brain)
4. force-load-* files require their plugin main file directly, bypassing active_plugins
5. apollo-route-setup runs its one-time maintenance on init @ 20
6. apollo-webp-force registers three image filters; nothing runs until an image is actually processed

apollo-brain.description: THE BRAIN. Earliest Apollo code to run. Defines APOLLO_REGISTRY_PATH, validates the runtime registry JSON parses, require_once apollo-core/apollo-core.php so Core registers its bootstrap before active_plugins is processed, installs the script defer filter, and wires registry/page cache purge.
does: json_decode validation of that file — logs to error_log only when WP_DEBUG_LOG, never die()s in production
script_loader_tag filter: adds defer to front-end scripts, with an explicit allow-list that must stay synchronous
transition_post_status @ 999 → apollo_purge_all() + Registry::clear_cache() on first publish only
does_not: Does NOT init CPT / Meta / FieldEncryption / HMAC / SEOTextBlock / PaneMode — apollo_core_bootstrap() on plugins_loaded P1 owns all of that, so ordering is guaranteed and nothing double-inits
Does NOT load the registry JSON into a constant — Apollo\Core\Registry + object cache own that, to avoid duplicating ~2.3 MB in RAM
defer_hard_exclusions: cdn.apollo.rio.br/v1(.x)/core.js — matched by regex on src
tags already carrying defer or async

apollo-debug.guard: WP_DEBUG || APOLLO_DEV_MODE — returns immediately otherwise, so production overhead is zero
apollo-debug.description: Query Monitor panel for the Apollo ecosystem plus the apollo_debug_log() helper. Loads after apollo-brain (alphabetical: brain < debug).
panel_shows: Registry path, load status, plugin count
Active Apollo plugins with version + status from the registry
Whether the registry came from object cache or disk
apollo-debug.$notable: Hooks plugins_loaded @ 0 to reset display_errors=0, because the third-party wp-debugging plugin calls @ini_set('display_errors',1) at load time and apollo-core's plugins_loaded @ 1 textdomain notice would otherwise corrupt REST JSON responses.

apollo-dev-routing.guard: APOLLO_DEV_MODE — early return at file level
apollo-dev-routing.description: On template_redirect, records which route handler won into $GLOBALS['apollo_dev_route_handler'] and logs it. Reads apollo_login_page / apollo_home_page / apollo_feed_page query vars and $GLOBALS['apollo_current_route'].

apollo-error-handler.description: Funnels 4xx/5xx through the central Apollo error pages so every plugin and WP core surface the same UX. Hooked last so each plugin still gets first chance to claim its route (e.g. apollo-login's virtual /acesso). Mirrors the Apache ErrorDocument directives in the project .htaccess.

apollo-events-helpers-guard.description: Brutal early guarantee that apollo_event_* global helpers exist before any template runs. Force-requires apollo-events main file if not already loaded, calls apollo_event_ensure_helpers(), and defines a fallback apollo_event_parse_date() (with hardcoded pt-BR month/weekday tables) if the real one is missing.
apollo-events-helpers-guard.$risk: Declares global functions with a pt-BR date table duplicated from apollo-events. If apollo-events changes its own parse_date contract, this shim silently keeps serving the old shape whenever the plugin fails to load. Shim, not a feature — retire once apollo-events is reliably active.

apollo-force-open-registration.description: Forces WordPress 'Anyone can register' to READ as enabled. Runs after Really Simple SSL (which filters the same option at 999).
apollo-force-open-registration.$risk: SECURITY-RELEVANT AND INVISIBLE. Overrides the effective value of users_can_register for every read, including REST and wp-admin. The DB option is untouched, so wp-admin shows 'checked' while the stored value may be '0' — anyone auditing the setting in the UI cannot tell it is being forced. Any decision to close registration MUST delete this file; unchecking the box in wp-admin will not work.

apollo-htaccess-lock.description: Restores and read-locks the root .htaccess before regular plugins (NFD / WP core) can truncate it. Thin loader: requires apollo-core/includes/htaccess-lock.php, which holds the real logic.

Do not edit; change the source under plugins/apollo-core/mu-plugins/apollo-htaccess-lock.php' — but the path it actually requires is includes/htaccess-lock.php. apollo-route-setup.description: One-time maintenance, gated on an option flag. Drafts WP Pages whose slugs collide with Apollo virtual routes, clears the Apollo Home template from conflicting pages, re-adds rewrite rules, flushes them, and clears Registry + FrontRouteDispatcher caches.

apollo-webp-force.description: Forces every image size WordPress generates to be written as WebP at quality 80, and prefers Imagick over GD. PHASE 1 ONLY: the uploaded original is deliberately untouched.
filters_hooked: jpeg_quality @ 10 => 82, for any JPEG still generated
actions_hooked: admin_notices — warns only when no editor can write WebP
does_not: Does NOT replace or delete the uploaded original. APOLLO_WEBP_REPLACE_ORIGINAL is defined but deliberately UNREAD until Phase 2.
Does NOT convert gif / webp / avif / svg / ico / bmp / tiff / pdf — by omission: only three keys are ever added to the format map.
Does NOT convert the site icon. WP favicon paths expect PNG, and a broken fallback there shows on every browser tab.
Does NOT register a CPT, meta key, option, REST route or admin page.
apollo-webp-force.$host_capability_2026_08_31: Verified from the live library rather than a probe: attachment 117 (club63-3.webp) carries a full generated WebP subsize set and attachment 187 (festa-selvagem.avif) carries a full AVIF set. WordPress can only produce those through WP_Image_Editor, so Imagick with WebP AND AVIF is live on apollo.rio.br.
apollo-webp-force.$why_mu: The filters do not need the MU layer to work — the format decision happens inside wp_generate_attachment_metadata(), far after plugins_loaded. MU is chosen so a half-converted library cannot be caused by someone deactivating a plugin in wp-admin.
apollo-webp-force.$risk: LOW while Phase 1 stands: three filters, no writes, no state. WordPress core adds its own guard — WP_Image_Editor::get_output_format() honours the mapping only when supports_mime_type() agrees — so an editor without WebP keeps JPEG instead of emitting a broken file. Re-grade this entry to MEDIUM when Phase 2 lands, because Phase 2 deletes originals.
apollo-webp-force.$phase: 1 of 6. Phase 2 (replace original), 3 (existing library via Tools -> Apollo Health), 4 (scope classified-* sizes), 5 (hardening) are not implemented yet.

$force_load_pattern.what: Four mu-plugin files each require a plugin's main file directly, bypassing the WordPress active_plugins option.
$force_load_pattern.why: Guarantees virtual routes and global helpers exist even when a plugin is not activated in wp-admin, or when activation state drifts between environments.
cost: wp-admin's Plugins screen no longer tells the truth: a force-loaded plugin runs whether it shows as active or not, and DEACTIVATING IT THERE DOES NOTHING.
register_activation_hook never fires on this path — a plugin that installs DB tables or seeds options on activation will run without them.
Load order moves from the plugins layer to the MU layer, which is earlier than some plugins expect.
$force_load_pattern.retire_when: The plugin is reliably present in production active_plugins. Three of the four files say so in their own headers.

$registry_path_warning.severity: HIGH — naming collision that has confused every reader of this registry
$registry_path_warning.problem: TWO different files are called apollo-registry.json.

runtime.purpose: What the SITE reads at request time.

documentation.purpose: The chaptered SSOT's build output. Documentation. NOT read at request time.

$registry_path_warning.relationship: The doc monolith is intended to be deployed to the runtime path — 00-registry-map.json build_rules.output.runtime names it, and build.js explicitly does NOT write it ('runtime target (deploy step, not written here)'). So the deploy step is manual and undocumented, and the two files can silently diverge.
$registry_path_warning.consequence: A chapter edit changes nothing at runtime until someone runs build.js --write AND copies the monolith to wp-content/. Neither step is automated or verified.
$registry_path_warning.$open_question: Nothing in this registry records WHEN the runtime file was last synced, or whether it currently matches the monolith. Add a deploy step, or a doctor check that diffs the two.
